pool.text: Around a circle are written \( 15 \) numbers, each equal to \( +1 \) or \( -1 \), with exactly \( 1 \) of them initially equal to \( -1 \). pool.sol: Negating \( 2 \) entries multiplies the total product \( P = \prod_{j=1}^{15} x_j \) by \( (-1)^{2} = +1 \). Since initially there are \( 1 \) (an odd number of) \( -1 \)'s, \( P = -1 \) forever, so we can never reach zero \( -1 \)'s! However, reducing pairs of \( -1 \)'s leaves a single \( -1 \) and \( 14 \) copies of \( +1 \), achieving maximum sum \( 14 - 1 = 13 \).
hints: Examine the parity of the count of \( -1 \)'s (equivalently, the product \( \prod x_j \)) when \( 2 \) signs are flipped.
Because \( 2 \) is even and \( 1 \) is odd, the number of \( -1 \)'s is always odd (at least \( 1 \)).
Verify a single \( -1 \) is achievable, giving maximum sum \( (15 - 1)(+1) + 1(-1) = 13 \).

Since initially there are \( 9 \) (an odd number of) \( -1 \)'s, \( P = -1 \) forever, so we can never reach zero \( -1 \)'s!
